"""Explain original Parameter totals on their different retained valid-cell supports.

Pure arithmetic over saved rows. This module opens no raster, runs no model and
does not replace any original change, percentage, area or range.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from copy import deepcopy
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import math
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = "upstate.parameter-support-reconciliation/v1"
EDITION = 1
JSON_FILE = "support-reconciliation.json"
CSV_FILE = "support-reconciliation.csv"
SOURCE_FILE = "parameter-support-reconciliation.py"
FILES = (JSON_FILE, CSV_FILE, SOURCE_FILE)
KEYS = ("case_id", "case", "run_id", "profile_id", "area_id", "area", "pollutant", "units")
MASS_KEYS = ("baseline_mass", "case_mass", "change", "baseline_full_mass", "case_full_mass")
COUNT_KEYS = ("baseline_valid_cells", "case_valid_cells", "paired_valid_cells")
DERIVED = (
    "baseline_only_cells", "case_only_cells", "baseline_only_area_ha", "case_only_area_ha",
    "baseline_common_fraction", "case_common_fraction", "independent_full_change",
    "baseline_only_mass_difference", "case_only_mass_difference",
    "paired_mass_difference", "stored_change_arithmetic_residual",
    "reconciliation_residual", "reconciliation_available", "unavailable_reason",
    "sign_reversal", "area_derivation_basis",
)
CSV_FIELDS = (
    "selected_row_index", "original_row_index", "original_artifact_sha256",
    "selected_row_pointer", "original_member", *KEYS, *COUNT_KEYS,
    "paired_area_ha", "pixel_area_ha", *MASS_KEYS, *DERIVED,
)
NOTES = [
    "Independent full change is case own-valid mass minus baseline own-valid mass. The stored paired change compares only cells valid in both runs. Both quantities remain distinct.",
    "Full change = stored paired change + case-only mass difference - baseline-only mass difference + reconciliation residual. Exclusive mass terms are arithmetic differences between each run's full and paired reductions, not a new raster aggregation.",
    "The explicit residual retains any disagreement between the original stored paired change and a subtraction of the two stored paired masses. Separately reduced floating-point quantities need not close exactly; small signed residuals are not clipped or interpreted as physical loss.",
    "Own-valid and paired counts define exclusive support. Missing cells are not zero export. With no paired cells, the original paired nulls remain null and no paired reconciliation or sign comparison is supplied.",
    "Exclusive hectares are derived only when the original row retains a finite positive pixel_area_ha. No nominal grid size is assumed. The original paired area is copied, not recalculated.",
    "An opposite sign describes these two saved summaries on different supports. It is not a restoration benefit, causal attribution, observed-load validation, confidence interval or four-case common-mask interaction.",
    "Every row retains the original result SHA256, case/run/profile/area/pollutant key and its selected-results.json row pointer. An original full-result row index is supplied only when that original index is actually available.",
]


def _finite(value, label, *, nullable=False):
    if value is None and nullable:
        return None
    if type(value) not in (int, float) or not math.isfinite(value):
        raise ValueError("Retain a finite original " + label)
    return value


def _difference(left, right):
    if left is None or right is None:
        return None
    value = math.fsum((left, -right))
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        raise ValueError("Support reconciliation exceeds finite arithmetic")
    return value


def _key(row):
    return tuple(row[name] for name in ("case_id", "area_id", "pollutant"))


def reconcile_row(row):
    """Return an independent projection; the caller's original row is untouched."""
    result = {name: deepcopy(row.get(name)) for name in KEYS}
    for name in MASS_KEYS:
        result[name] = _finite(row.get(name), name, nullable=True)
    for name in COUNT_KEYS:
        value = row.get(name)
        if type(value) is not int or value < 0:
            raise ValueError("Retain an original nonnegative integer " + name)
        result[name] = value
    paired, baseline, case = (result[name] for name in
                             ("paired_valid_cells", "baseline_valid_cells", "case_valid_cells"))
    if paired > min(baseline, case):
        raise ValueError("Original paired cells exceed their own-valid support")
    result["paired_area_ha"] = _finite(row.get("paired_area_ha"), "paired area", nullable=True)
    area = row.get("pixel_area_ha")
    known_area = type(area) in (int, float) and math.isfinite(area) and area > 0
    result.update(
        pixel_area_ha=area if known_area else None,
        baseline_only_cells=baseline - paired, case_only_cells=case - paired,
        baseline_only_area_ha=(baseline - paired) * area if known_area else None,
        case_only_area_ha=(case - paired) * area if known_area else None,
        baseline_common_fraction=paired / baseline if baseline else None,
        case_common_fraction=paired / case if case else None,
        area_derivation_basis=("exclusive original cell count times original pixel_area_ha"
                               if known_area else "original positive pixel area unavailable"),
        independent_full_change=_difference(result["case_full_mass"], result["baseline_full_mass"]),
        baseline_only_mass_difference=None, case_only_mass_difference=None,
        paired_mass_difference=None, stored_change_arithmetic_residual=None,
        reconciliation_residual=None, reconciliation_available=False,
        unavailable_reason=None, sign_reversal=None,
    )
    if not paired:
        result["unavailable_reason"] = "no_paired_valid_cells"
    elif any(result[name] is None for name in MASS_KEYS):
        result["unavailable_reason"] = "original_mass_or_change_unavailable"
    else:
        baseline_only = _difference(result["baseline_full_mass"], result["baseline_mass"])
        case_only = _difference(result["case_full_mass"], result["case_mass"])
        paired_difference = _difference(result["case_mass"], result["baseline_mass"])
        residual = math.fsum((result["independent_full_change"], -result["change"],
                              -case_only, baseline_only))
        result.update(
            baseline_only_mass_difference=baseline_only, case_only_mass_difference=case_only,
            paired_mass_difference=paired_difference,
            stored_change_arithmetic_residual=_difference(result["change"], paired_difference),
            reconciliation_residual=residual, reconciliation_available=True,
            sign_reversal=((result["change"] < 0 < result["independent_full_change"])
                           or (result["independent_full_change"] < 0 < result["change"])),
        )
    for value in result.values():
        if type(value) is float and not math.isfinite(value):
            raise ValueError("Support reconciliation contains a nonfinite derived quantity")
    return result


def calculate(selected, rows, *, original_rows=None):
    """Bind every selected row without paging or parsing another native artifact."""
    choice = selected["selection"]
    artifact = choice["expected_artifact_sha256"]
    if (not isinstance(artifact, str) or len(artifact) != 64
            or any(letter not in "0123456789abcdef" for letter in artifact)):
        raise ValueError("Retain the exact original Parameter artifact SHA256")
    original_indices = None
    if original_rows is not None:
        original_indices = {_key(row): index for index, row in enumerate(original_rows)}
        if len(original_indices) != len(original_rows):
            raise ValueError("Original result repeats a case/area/pollutant key")
    archived = choice.get("source_basis") == "saved_parameter_result_archive"
    member = "original-result.json" if archived else "original-study/results.json"
    calculated, seen = [], set()
    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
        key = _key(row)
        if key in seen:
            raise ValueError("Selected reconciliation rows repeat an original identity")
        seen.add(key)
        if original_indices is not None and key not in original_indices:
            raise ValueError("Selected reconciliation row is absent from the original result")
        item = reconcile_row(row)
        item.update(
            selected_row_index=index,
            original_row_index=original_indices[key] if original_indices is not None else None,
            original_artifact_sha256=artifact,
            selected_row_pointer="selected-results.json#/rows/" + str(index),
            original_member=member,
        )
        calculated.append(item)
    return {
        "schema": SCHEMA, "edition": EDITION, "selection": deepcopy(choice),
        "source_basis": choice.get("source_basis", "saved_parameter_study"),
        "original_artifact_sha256": artifact, "original_member": member,
        "original_row_index_basis": ("original complete result array" if original_indices is not None
                                     else "not loaded; retained original row key and selected row pointer"),
        "rows": calculated, "notes": list(NOTES),
    }


def _table(columns, rows):
    return {"kind": "table", "columns": columns, "rows": rows, "widths": None}


def _show(value):
    return "Unavailable" if value is None else value


def sections(selected, rows):
    """Use the existing observed-report table/link contract, with original units."""
    packet = calculate(selected, rows)
    positions = {key: index + 1 for index, key in enumerate(selected["selection"]["case_ids"])}
    blocks = [*NOTES, {"kind": "links", "items": [
        {"title": "Complete support reconciliation and original row bindings", "path": JSON_FILE},
        {"title": "All derived support-accounting rows (CSV)", "path": CSV_FILE},
        {"title": "Exact support-accounting implementation", "path": SOURCE_FILE},
    ]}]
    result = [["Accounting for different native valid-cell support", blocks]]
    for area in selected["areas"]:
        for pollutant in selected["selection"]["pollutants"]:
            chosen = [row for row in packet["rows"]
                      if row["area_id"] == area["id"] and row["pollutant"] == pollutant]
            for offset in range(0, len(chosen), 60):
                page = chosen[offset:offset + 60]
                title = area["name"] + " / " + pollutant.replace("_export", "") + " — support accounting"
                if len(chosen) > 60:
                    title += " / rows " + str(offset + 1) + "–" + str(offset + len(page))
                result.append([title, [
                    "These are arithmetic projections of the unchanged saved rows. All mass columns "
                    "retain the stated annual mass unit. The original paired change remains authoritative.",
                    _table(["Position", "Units", "Stored paired change", "Plus case-only mass",
                            "Minus baseline-only mass", "Plus residual", "Equals own-valid full change"], [
                        [positions[row["case_id"]], row["units"], _show(row["change"]),
                         _show(row["case_only_mass_difference"]), _show(row["baseline_only_mass_difference"]),
                         _show(row["reconciliation_residual"]), _show(row["independent_full_change"])]
                        for row in page]),
                    _table(["Position", "Common cells", "Baseline-only cells", "Case-only cells",
                            "Opposite nonzero signs", "Unavailable reconciliation reason"], [
                        [positions[row["case_id"]], row["paired_valid_cells"], row["baseline_only_cells"],
                         row["case_only_cells"], _show(row["sign_reversal"]),
                         row["unavailable_reason"] or "Available"] for row in page]),
                ]])
    reversals = [row for row in packet["rows"] if row["sign_reversal"] is True]
    if reversals:
        original = {_key(row): row for row in rows}
        example = min(reversals, key=lambda row: len(original[_key(row)].get("overrides", {})))
        result.append(["Why the direction can change with the support", [
            example["case"] + " / " + example["pollutant"] + " / " + example["area"] +
            " is an original saved example. A single changed assumption is preferred when available; "
            "the selected rows and figure order are unchanged.",
            _table(["Arithmetic term", "Meaning", example["units"]], [
                ["Stored paired change", "Case minus baseline on the same valid cells", example["change"]],
                ["Plus case-only mass", "Case full total minus case paired total",
                 example["case_only_mass_difference"]],
                ["Minus baseline-only mass", "Baseline full total minus baseline paired total",
                 example["baseline_only_mass_difference"]],
                ["Plus arithmetic residual", "Preserved separate-reduction difference",
                 example["reconciliation_residual"]],
                ["Equals own-valid full change", "Case full total minus baseline full total",
                 example["independent_full_change"]],
            ]),
            _table(["Original support", "Cells", "Area (ha)"], [
                ["Common", example["paired_valid_cells"], _show(example["paired_area_ha"])],
                ["Valid only in baseline", example["baseline_only_cells"], _show(example["baseline_only_area_ha"])],
                ["Valid only in case", example["case_only_cells"], _show(example["case_only_area_ha"])],
            ]),
            "The two signs describe different supports, not conflicting model calculations. "
            "Neither summary replaces the other. These aggregate records do not identify the cause "
            "of every excluded cell, establish one common mask across all parameter cases, or "
            "turn this parameter comparison into a measured restoration benefit.",
            _table(["Original source binding", "Retained identity"], [
                ["Selected source row", example["selected_row_pointer"]],
                ["Original result SHA256", packet["original_artifact_sha256"]],
                ["Original case", example["case_id"]], ["Original run", example["run_id"]],
                ["Original profile", example["profile_id"]], ["Original area", example["area_id"]],
            ]),
        ]])
    return result


def write(directory, selected, rows, *, original_rows=None, origin_uri=""):
    """Retain complete derived projections before the existing source inventory."""
    from .common import atomic_bytes, atomic_json
    directory = Path(directory)
    packet = calculate(selected, rows, original_rows=original_rows)
    body = Path(__file__).read_bytes()
    packet["implementation"] = {
        "path": SOURCE_FILE, "bytes": len(body), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()}
    packet["origin_uri"] = origin_uri
    atomic_json(directory / JSON_FILE, packet, immutable=True)
    stream = io.StringIO(newline="")
    writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=CSV_FIELDS)
    writer.writeheader()
    for row in packet["rows"]:
        # Preserve numeric negatives; neutralize only textual spreadsheet formulae.
        writer.writerow({name: ("'" + row[name] if isinstance(row[name], str)
                               and row[name].startswith(("=", "+", "-", "@", "\t", "\r"))
                               else row[name]) for name in CSV_FIELDS})
    atomic_bytes(directory / CSV_FILE, stream.getvalue().encode("utf-8"), immutable=True)
    atomic_bytes(directory / SOURCE_FILE, body, immutable=True)
    return packet

# Parameter support reconciliation

This is a derived explanation of already-saved Parameter results. It is included by both maintained scientific-source producers: `model.parameter_report_source` for an editable local Parameter study and `model.parameter_archive_source` for an original completed result archive. The existing PDF, HTML, Markdown and source-package paths render the same sections.

It does not open a raster or execute a model. Original result bytes, selected row values, percentages, sensitivity values, figures, ranges and scientific selections remain unchanged. The new JSON/CSV explicitly identify their arithmetic as derived.

## The two questions answered by the original totals

A Parameter row retains the baseline and case totals on each run's own valid cells, and their totals on the cells valid in both runs. Define:

- `Bfull`, `Cfull`: original baseline and case own-valid masses.
- `Bpair`, `Cpair`: original masses on that pair's common valid cells.
- `Dpair`: the original stored paired change, with the producer's original sign convention: case minus baseline.
- `Bonly = Bfull - Bpair` and `Conly = Cfull - Cpair`: differences of the retained reductions.
- `Dfull = Cfull - Bfull`: derived own-valid full change.
- `residual = Dfull - Dpair - Conly + Bonly`.

The complete accounting identity is:

```text
own-valid full change
  = stored common-cell change
  + case-only mass difference
  - baseline-only mass difference
  + arithmetic residual
```

The term “mass difference” is deliberate: this helper subtracts original reductions and does not independently aggregate exclusive-cell rasters. The residual records the effects of separately stored/reduced floating-point values; the original paired change is never overwritten by a new subtraction. The companion also retains `stored_change_arithmetic_residual = Dpair - (Cpair - Bpair)`.

A lower common-cell export can coexist with a higher own-valid total when enough mass occurs on cells only valid in the case. Neither total replaces the other. Missing cells are not zero export, and an excluded-cell difference does not identify the reason those cells were excluded. This explanation does not establish a common mask across all parameter cases, conditional factorial effects, causal restoration effects, measured-load validation or statistical uncertainty.

## Counts, areas and missing quantities

Exclusive cell counts are original own-valid counts minus the original paired count. Common fractions use each run's own-valid cell count as its denominator.

Exclusive hectares are derived only from an original finite, positive `pixel_area_ha`; no nominal resolution is assumed. The original paired hectares are copied unchanged. When pixel area is unavailable, the exclusive areas remain null, with an explicit basis.

When paired support is empty, original paired masses remain null, the reconciliation and sign comparison are unavailable, and `unavailable_reason=no_paired_valid_cells`. A retained full-total difference can still be shown with its own meaning. Missing original masses or stored changes similarly produce `original_mass_or_change_unavailable`. Zero changes are not classified as opposite signs. Negative or small residuals are retained rather than clipped.

Units remain the original row's annual mass units; nitrogen, phosphorus and sediment are not summed together. The source sections group rows by original area and pollutant and preserve the selected case order.

## Original source identity and portable outputs

Every newly prepared scientific source includes:

- `support-reconciliation.json`: all derived rows, original selection, result SHA256, row keys, assumptions, null reasons and exact implementation identity.
- `support-reconciliation.csv`: the full flat projection, including original masses and counts, derived terms and source bindings.
- `parameter-support-reconciliation.py`: the exact implementation used for the projection.

Each row retains the original result SHA256, case/run/profile/area/pollutant identities and a `selected-results.json#/rows/N` pointer. The archive source additionally retains the actual original complete-result row index. The paged live source records the original composite row key without inventing a global array index.

The live source references `original-study/results.json`; the archive source references its byte-exact `original-result.json`. Both keep their original source basis. Report operation identities pin this helper's SHA256 alongside their existing producer and figure identities. The ordinary immutable companion inventory includes the two derived files and exact helper before source import, so the existing scientific-source/project transfer carries them. An updated helper produces another immutable source edition; old source reports remain readable.

The shared section producer still ends with `Original files and spatial interpretation`. The archive adapter replaces that live-source-specific appendix through its existing checked seam. Reconciliation sections precede it and are shared by both routes.

## Actual original Gura example

The retained input is `receiving/gura-original-four-case-results.json`, 17,291 bytes, SHA256:

`20a0f25d11742011784ac3bcae7857de108b244adaee8ceae7a79f9a921eaa9b`

The source retains 456,304 common cells, 2,663 baseline-only cells and 14,915 case-only cells. # Saved native case console

Open **Parameter studies → saved study → Native case console** on an original case. The console works for cases created or executed through the original Gura command-line course and for cases supervised by the operator.

The first section reads the maintained native run journal and its actual execution lock. It shows the current phase, selected native model stages, retained source stages and available space on the run filesystem. A running workspace coordinator is shown separately from the selected case, so an old completed case does not imply that the remaining cohort has stopped.

## Original attempts and logs

The attempt table combines the two existing receipt families:

| Entrypoint | Retained original source |
| --- | --- |
| Operator worker | `runs/<run_id>/supervision/<execution_id>/` |
| Gura isolated case | `gura-receiving/native-case-processes/<run_id>/<attempt_id>/` |

Every request must select the same project and native run. Operator requests also retain the exact native selection and their original request digest. Gura receipts retain their original request-body hash when published by the current course. Historical request paths remain provenance when a Workspace is transferred; physical reads resolve inside the reopened Workspace.

Choose **Open attempt** to inspect that retained worker or command-line invocation. The original native model log spans all attempts of its native run. **Worker process**, **stdout** and **stderr** select the separate process logs that actually exist for the chosen entrypoint. Reads start at the last64KiB; **Read from start** reads the same original file from its beginning. Each request reads at most64KiB, and the browser keeps a limited visible tail while the full file remains retained.

**Follow latest attempt** returns to the newest original receipt. Attempt pages have25 rows; changing pages does not change the selected attempt. **Refresh saved status** controls polling. Closing the dialog, replacing it or changing Workspace prevents a stale response from updating another view.

The selected resource observation keeps its original observing process and timestamp. Operator heartbeats describe the owned worker. The isolated course's after-return observation comes from its supervisor and is labeled accordingly. Group memory event counts include other processes sharing the cgroup. Only the original interruption record identifies an observed signal or counter difference; this console does not infer a cause from a large memory value or lifetime counter.

## Continue the same saved work

**Resume remaining study cases** submits the existing `parameter-study.run` action with the original saved study ID. It remains unavailable while the selected run, its workspace batch coordinator, or the same study's operator task is active. The original engine verifies completed cases and resumes its unfinished work.

Where the retained worker's task exists in the current operator, **Open original operator task** opens that task and its existing calculation console, Stop and reconnect controls. This is the way to reconnect an already-owned worker. Original CLI operations continue through their maintained command and operation owner.

**Download case record** exports the selected run status, original case binding, current history page, selected request/receipts, resource observations and bounded displayed log. The complete source files remain in the original Workspace and its normal portable archive.

For Tim: open a case to see what the original calculation actually did, read its saved output, and continue the same study without rebuilding its scientific selection.

## Native receiving

Use the existing equipped GURA-NATIVE-01 Workspace and its retained partial study. The API calls the maintained `native_execution.inspect_execution` and `parameter_studies.native_case_context`; it performs no model execution or saved-state mutation.

From the product root, compile the changed Python sources with the equipped interpreter:
```python
from pathlib import Path
for name in ("model/parameter_case_status.py", "operator/parameter_study_api.py", "operator/server.py"):
    compile(Path(name).read_bytes(), name, "exec")
```

Open an actual retained isolated case, compare its request/return hash and stdout/stderr text to the same original files, select an earlier attempt, and reopen the same study. The original run IDs, case selections and all source/stage/output descriptors remain unchanged.

# Read large saved parameter-study results

Open **Parameter studies → Open study → Results and downloads**. The result table reads the selected original result JSON in pages of 100 rows. Filter by reporting area or pollutant, use Previous/Next, or enter an original filtered row number in Go to result row.

The range table has its own Previous ranges / Next ranges controls. These are the exact saved minimum/maximum records over completed cases with matching spatial support. Paging does not recalculate a range or substitute the visible result page for the complete compared cohort.

The displayed source SHA256 identifies the retained scientific summary. If another completed summary is published while this view is open, the next read returns the new identity and starts both pagers at zero. Any now-unavailable filter is cleared. The current study's original run, parameter selections and completed-case history remain intact.

## First read and continued reads

The first result read builds a derivative SQLite index under:

    experiments/<study-id>/result-queries/<source-query-id>.sqlite

It streams the original UTF-8 JSON, validates the complete file against the retained byte count and SHA256, and records only row byte spans, original filter identities and row hashes. It does not make a second copy of the scientific matrix.

Later pages seek directly into the same original result file. Every returned row's body hash and area/pollutant identity must match the indexed span. File replacement, in-place changes and a changed saved result descriptor invalidate the observation.

The first build takes the original study lock and a derivative index lock. If the study is currently publishing results, reopen the table after that operation. A completed index can be read while a later calculation runs; a concurrent summary replacement requires a fresh page read.

A build checkpoints completed JSON values in batches. After interruption, the next request resumes from its saved parser position. It rereads the already-consumed byte prefix and requires its exact saved prefix hash before reusing any indexed spans. A repaired or replaced prefix rebuilds only the derivative checkpoint. It then continues parsing and indexing the remaining values, finishing the original whole-file hash. It never reruns a model or changes a scientific result.

The derivative is published only after the entire original JSON matches its retained source descriptor. A temporary partial index is not a completed result. The full scientific file and all original downloads remain authoritative.

## Transfer and reopen

The ordinary complete Workspace inventory retains the optional index and any partial checkpoint along with the scientific result. On a restored host, changed file identity causes a one-time complete original-byte verification before the saved byte spans are reused. If there is no index, the reader creates it from the original JSON.

The index format is versioned independently of the original model result. Updating this reader creates a separate derivative identity; original reports, JSON, CSV and GIS downloads keep their established paths and contents.

## API

The existing endpoint remains:

    GET /api/parameter-studies/results?workspace=...&id=...

Existing area_id, pollutant, offset and limit retain their meaning. New optional fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| range_offset | Original filtered range offset, starting at zero. |
| range_limit | Number of ranges, 1–1000. Omission returns all matching ranges from range_offset; the default offset zero retains the earlier complete matching-range response. |
| expected_artifact_sha256 | Previously displayed result identity. A changed edition resets both offsets and returns edition_changed=true. |

Response additions include total_ranges, filtered_ranges, range_offset, range_limit, artifact_bytes, query_edition and effective area_id/pollutant. saved_study_state/progress come from the current bound execution checkpoint; completed_cases/total_cases and scientific quantities remain from the selected original result edition.

Result reads validate the saved study specification and its original checkpoint, then read the retained result descriptor. They do not reopen every native run merely to page an existing scientific summary. The full study inspection and Native case console retain their original live-run semantics.

## Original receiving

At the existing equipped application's safe source boundary, use the actual saved study ID whose original results.json already exists:

    from model.workspace import Workspace
    from model.parameter_result_query import DEFAULT_RESULTS

    workspace = Workspace(actual_workspace)
    first = DEFAULT_RESULTS.read(workspace, actual_study_id, limit=100, range_limit=100)
    following = DEFAULT_RESULTS.read(
        workspace, actual_study_id, offset=100, limit=100,
        range_limit=100, expected_artifact_sha256=first["artifact_sha256"])

Compare returned rows to the corresponding original JSON slices using the actual retained file. Reopen the same study in the current operator, page its rows and ranges, then use the unchanged original full-result downloads. This reads the existing native cohort and starts no new scientific calculation.

# Continue an interrupted native parameter study

Open the saved **Parameter studies** item. **Run all cases** or **Resume remaining cases** uses the existing native calculation supervisor, with one fresh worker for each unfinished native run. Open that task's **Open calculation console** to read the original process log, resources and current native stage, request a stop, or reconnect after reopening the operator.

Completed native cases keep their original run IDs and verified outputs. Native stages already finished inside an incomplete run remain available to the original stage-reuse path. Changing execution isolation does not change a scientific selection, model parameter, grid, source body, comparison support or model version.

## A worker stopped unexpectedly

A directly observed negative child exit code is retained with its exact signal number/name. A reconnected worker that has disappeared without a completed result is retained as an interruption with an unavailable exit code. The coordinator stops this attempt before starting another case; it does not cascade through the remaining study or programme.

The saved study shows the original failure and recovery text. Its technical interruption details retain the request digest, native run, process ID, original process directory and available resource observations. A completed run remains complete even if its child receives a signal while exiting.

When both snapshots identify the same visible cgroup, the record contains measured differences in `memory.events` and `memory.events.local`. A rising `oom_kill` or `oom_group_kill` counter establishes an OOM-kill event in that shared group during the attempt. The counter does not identify which process was killed. A signal exit alone is not classified as an OOM kill.

Use the existing host's process and memory observations to reconcile capacity or the original external stop. Then choose **Resume remaining cases** on that saved study. No manual status editing or new scientific selection is required. **Refresh completed results** remains available for the retained completed cases.

## Reopen while the old worker is still running

The worker retains the original native batch lease after its operator process closes. Reopening the saved study reconnects that worker before acquiring the lease for the coordinator. The same request and original case binding are checked in both supervisor and worker. A different native batch cannot take that lease while the existing case continues.

Stop requests and operator shutdown pass through the maintained supervisor. A requested stop reaches that calculation's original process group. Closing the operator lets the native worker continue; reopening its task reconnects it. The original study coordinator retains its partial progress at that boundary.

## Existing Gura course

Continue the original GURA-NATIVE-01 Workspace and source edition. The maintained `source_tools/receive_gura_studies.py --isolate-native-cases` entrypoint keeps its existing suite and child lock inheritance. An observed child signal now leaves the suite partial, with exact process and interruption receipts under `gura-receiving/native-case-processes/<run-id>/<attempt>/`.

The suite's saved `state.json` contains `continue_argv`: the actual interpreter, application, Workspace, original input directory, baseline run, scopes, design, resolved evaluation-run IDs and original output options. Run that argument array through the equipped owner's existing operation after reconciling capacity. It resolves the earlier planning selection to its original evaluation IDs, so later edits to planning state cannot silently choose another suite.

A retained complete original baseline, completed NDR cases, SDR stages and existing reports all remain in place. Interruption handling performs no additional native calculation or source transformation. Existing study, programme and supervisor records remain part of the original portable Workspace.

## Source and installation

Receive the complete current application containing `model/native_execution.py`, `model/parameter_studies.py`, `model/native_worker.py`, `operator/native_jobs.py`, `operator/parameter_study_jobs.py`, the parameter-study API and original worker console. The new adapter uses only the existing standard-library/native application dependencies.

For the existing equipped course, first compile the changed Python modules in memory from their actual files. Reopen an already completed saved study and confirm its original case/run selections and current report. Continue the existing unfinished course through the same task or saved CLI argument array, retaining its actual command, process receipt and first result. The completed-course and original case identity are the receiving basis.

**For Tim:** Reopen the saved study, read the interruption if present, and choose Resume remaining cases after the current host is ready; completed native results stay available.

### Reopening a worker that ended while the operator was closed

The first continuation reconciles the original worker request before a replacement
can launch. A disappeared worker with no result retains an unavailable exit code
and an interruption receipt; it does not acquire a guessed signal or OOM cause.
After reviewing the actual capacity and receipt, use the same saved study's run
control again. That explicit retry may replace the recorded failed attempt while
retaining its original request and completed cases. A completed owned worker is
allowed to exit before the coordinator reacquires its inherited batch lease.

# Saved parameter-study case browsing

Open **Parameter studies → Open study**. The original saved study now opens its case page and current whole-study progress without repeatedly loading every native stage registry.

## Cases and recovery

Use **Case state** to select all, unfinished, failed, interrupted or completed cases. **Find a case** searches the retained case ID, label, native run ID, parameter profile ID and original parameter changes. Search applies to the complete saved study. Previous, Next and Go to case navigate the matching cases in their original order; the displayed study total remains the complete original inventory.

**Native case console** opens the selected run's actual worker or CLI attempts, retained logs and exit receipts. Its saved-study binding is checked against the original specification and exact case selection. Opening a case does not inspect unrelated native stage registries.

Study activity and native-run activity are separate observations. A recorded running case whose original run lock is free is displayed as interrupted. A saved study marked complete becomes visibly partial if a native case is no longer complete. Completed cases and actual version labels remain the original native observations. Run all cases / Resume remaining cases retain the original study ID and existing execution queue; filter or page choices do not change the scientific run selection.

A page is a read of ongoing original records, not a simultaneous snapshot of all child processes. The whole-study counts observe every original run record and lock on each request. The native console retains the detailed selected process and source histories.

## Original result editions and complete selections

Result rows and ranges continue through the original source-bound result index. Original JSON, CSV, raster and report downloads keep the full scientific outputs. Download tickets follow the displayed result artifact SHA even when a newer completed summary appears while the study is open.

Use as new draft retains the complete original study selection, including all explicit parameter axes and reporting-area choices. Use completed cases in calibration continues through the original complete candidate API. Neither operation derives a scientific cohort from a visible page.

## Native read API

The additive model reader is `model.parameter_views.DEFAULT_VIEWS`.

`read(workspace, study_id, offset=0, limit=50, case_filter="all", query="", run_id=None)` returns the original study metadata plus:

- `cases`: the selected original page, retaining overrides, profiles, original native selections and completed model versions;
- `case_count` and `progress`: counts for the full study;
- `page`: effective offset/limit, filtered total, original study total, state filter and search;
- `active` and `native_active`: current original study and run lock observations;
- `recorded_state`: the saved coordinator state, separate from the visible interrupted/partial state;
- `cases_complete`: whether this response contains the entire original case inventory.

A zero limit reads metadata/counts without returning cases. Positive page sizes are at most500; this limits the response size, not the study design. A supplied original run ID returns its exact saved case bindings. Full scientific inspection remains `model.parameter_studies.inspect`, and the original operator `/api/item?kind=parameter-studies` continues returning that complete inspection.

The operator's additive `GET /api/parameter-studies/view` accepts id, offset, limit, case_filter, query and run_id. It attaches the existing native download tickets. The shared execution console endpoint retains its original options and response contracts.

## Read throughput and source identity

The reader uses the existing bounded `ProjectedFileCache`:32MiB of isolated saved specification/checkpoint projections and16MiB of native projections. These are process-local byte budgets, not limits on scientific studies or cases. Oversized or evicted records are read normally.

Each native cache miss applies the same original run-selection digest and completed-stage validation as Workspace.inspect_run before keeping only selection, state, errors and native version metadata. Exact original frozen selections, legacy requested versions and the baseline identity are checked against each saved case on every read. Replacing an original JSON record invalidates its projection by file identity. Live locks are observed afresh and are never inferred from a cached timestamp.

The reader writes no source, run or study records and starts no calculation. Scientific execution, comparison math, calibration, complete result exports and original portable source inventories remain in their maintained producers.

# Parameter studies in SourceReports

Open **Parameter studies**, open a saved study, and choose **Prepare scientific source**. This uses the saved result edition already produced by the study. The original native run, parameter profile, grid, land-cover scenario and reporting polygons remain its scientific basis.

## Choose the report

Name the report source. Leave **All completed cases in this result** selected to present the complete saved cohort. To choose a subset, select **Choose original cases**. Search by case, profile, native run or parameter assignment; use the paged case list to select across pages. **Select matching cases** adds every matching original case, including off-page cases. **Clear selected cases** empties the explicit selection. Returning to all cases preserves the stored explicit choices for later editing, while the submitted report uses all cases.

Select one or more original reporting areas and pollutants. The prepared source retains each case ID, run ID, profile ID, parameter assignment, original polygon selection and original source edition. A **Report this case** button beside a completed native case starts the same selection with that case chosen. If that case completed after the last summary, first use **Refresh completed results**.

**Prepare scientific source** submits one action to the existing native operator queue. Preparation freezes the complete original exported study files and selected numeric rows. The task opens the original study and offers **Compose selected scientific report**, plus the ordinary scientific PDF, HTML, Markdown and ZIP downloads. The composer uses the shared SourceReports renderer and can combine this source with other original sources in the chosen order.

From the saved study, **Open prepared source in composer** reopens the most recently prepared source. The task button carries its exact source-operation ID, so reopening an earlier task selects that exact earlier result and subset even after another source was prepared. If no source exists, prepare one first.

## Read the original quantities

Every displayed change is **case minus baseline**, on the original paired valid cells. The source presents paired quantities and support counts alongside independent full totals. A zero baseline leaves percentage change undefined. A case with no valid paired support retains undefined quantities.

Full-study minimum/maximum ranges appear only when every completed case in that saved result is selected. Selecting fewer cases preserves their original rows and omits the full-cohort range from the selected presentation. The complete original results file still retains every published range. Source preparation performs no new scientific aggregation or native calculation.

The selected report can have fewer cases than the original study. Its introduction separately states original total cases, completed cases in the result and selected cases, areas and pollutants. All physical constituents remain separate, in their original annual-mass units.

## Map and source navigation

**View difference maps** opens the actual retained comparison in Spatial review. **Open difference maps** opens its original comparison record. Both refer to the original full comparison extent. Selecting a reporting polygon for the scientific report does not clip or replace a native GeoTIFF.

The source package includes the complete original study report and export members, original requested maps, native arguments, execution-version records, aggregation context and any adopted aggregation ancestry. It also retains the selected coefficient-table originals with companions, selected reporting-polygon originals, original grid record, reporting/model-domain geometry when available, and an inventory of the larger native inputs retained in the full Workspace.

Use the SourceReports original-source export for an independently importable source edition. Use the complete Workspace transfer when the recipient will continue original native calculations or inspect the large original/aligned input and output rasters.

## Saved editions and continuation

The selection is bound to the exact original results SHA256. If results change between reviewing the form and queue execution, the operation asks for a new review instead of silently selecting the new result. Existing prepared sources remain available through their original task and imported source IDs.

Preparation retains independent file copies, exact export-manifest descriptors and immutable selected rows. It can continue interrupted preparation of the same source operation. Once the original source is registered, a renderer interruption can resume without rerunning the scientific model.

## Native API

Existing queued action:

    parameter-study.source.prepare

Payload:

    {
      "experiment_id": "<original-study-id>",
      "expected_artifact_sha256": "<saved-results-sha256>",
      "title": "Selected Parameter study",
      "case_ids": null,
      "area_ids": ["reporting-area"],
      "pollutants": ["nitrogen_export", "phosphorus_export"],
      "render": true
    }

Null case/area/pollutant selections mean all original available choices. Explicit lists must be nonempty, unique and part of that result. Original producer order is retained.

Read endpoints:

- GET /api/parameter-studies/source-catalog?id=STUDY_ID
- GET /api/parameter-studies/scientific-source?id=STUDY_ID
- GET /api/parameter-studies/scientific-source?source_id=SOURCE_OPERATION_ID

The first read returns original choices and the current result identity. The second opens the latest prepared source for the study. The third opens an exact saved source operation. All reads use the selected Workspace.

The additive model API is model.parameter_report_source.catalog, preview, prepare, latest and get. The original parameter-study kernel, result index, full exports, ensemble source producer and shared collector/renderer remain authoritative.

## Receiving inspection

Use a real saved native study with both completed and pending cases, multiple reporting areas when available, and its actual difference maps. Operate the exact current application at desktop and narrow widths: open the report form, search beyond its first case page, select across pages, change between all/explicit choices, select areas/pollutants, prepare, open the exact task source in the composer, render all offered formats, follow original map/source links, then reopen the Workspace and earlier source task. Inspect the actual PDF pages and original report links as well as populated/empty/error states. Retain the original study and source IDs in the existing native operation's response.

Source and V8 controller checks support this implementation; actual rendered desktop/mobile/report inspection belongs to the equipped receiving application.


## Original-result figures

Prepared sources include separate monochrome figures for each selected reporting area, pollutant and original unit. Each page shows at most twelve original cases, with a position-to-case key immediately after the figure. One panel shows the original baseline/case annual masses on that pair's valid cells; the next shows the retained case-minus-baseline change around a visible zero line. Cases are points rather than a connected trend.

Changed support has a separate marker and legend entry. Each figure includes the original independent baseline and case cell counts, paired cells and paired area. Matching counts alone do not establish identical geography across different cases. The paired values retain their original comparison support; the original full totals remain distinct in the numeric report.

Undefined values have no plotted point. The coverage record retains the exact field, original case and source-row pointer for each omission. A page containing only undefined original values produces no empty quantitative plot; those cases remain in the report's original tables and coverage files.

The shared scientific renderer uses the same numeric figure specification for vector PDF graphics and ordinary report exports; standalone SVGs remain source companions. The complete coordinate CSV and JSON retain the original result SHA256, selected-results SHA256, source JSON pointer, case/profile/run identities, parameter assignments and support metadata. Ordinal case positions and padded axis bounds are presentation metadata. No fitting, interpolation, averaging, physical conversion or probabilistic interval is introduced.

Inspect each actual PDF/HTML figure, case key and support table at receiving. Check units, zero line, undefined coverage, changed-support markers, page boundaries and original source links. Open the standalone SVG, coordinate CSV/JSON and original numeric result from the delivered source before approving that outgoing report. Earlier prepared sources remain independently reopenable; preparing under the figure edition creates another source operation from the same original scientific result.


## Original input declarations and geographic scope

The report opens with the retained native grid and its original computational-domain and reporting-geography selections. Raster-envelope area is labeled separately from the geometry selected for modeled quantities. The original CRS, cell size, upstream buffer and domain reason travel with the report; selecting a smaller reporting polygon changes the presented original rows and leaves the native grid unchanged.

Source classifications come from the retained input entries. A simulated declaration remains simulated after adopting a completed Ensemble into Parameter studies; absent classifications are displayed as not declared. The existing SAME5156 square and the separate actual Upper Savannah geographic edition keep their original identities.

The report retains the fixed land-cover scenario, complete original source-collection records and manifests, and exact profile references. Explicitly referenced assumption, recipe and matched-control documents are copied with their original hashes and companions through the shared source-scope collector. Original input-accounting and control declarations remain distinct from native annual export results. Long source statements appear after the quantitative tables; links to their exact original documents remain in the opening source section.

The source package includes `study-source-scope.json`, original grid/scenario/source records, referenced document bodies, selected coefficient tables and reporting geometries. Its inventory identifies larger native raster and scenario-mask bodies held by the full Workspace without duplicating those bodies into the report. The source operation binds the exact scope-helper implementation as well as the original result, producer and figure helpers. Preparing a current source creates its own immutable edition; earlier source IDs, tasks and downloads continue to reopen their original reports.

At receiving, open the actual report's geographic/source declarations and follow its original-grid, source-scope and document links. For an adopted scenario study, confirm its fixed scenario title and native run IDs against the original Ensemble, then compare the unchanged annual-mass tables and figures with the retained result rows. The native model and paired aggregation are unchanged by this source presentation.

# Native calculation console and process recovery

Operation ES-SUPERVISION-20261012 adds a native calculation console to the maintained Upper Savannah operator. Start the same saved run through the existing Run original models action. The existing Workspace remains the source of the selected grid, parameter profile, land-cover scenario, original InVEST execution, retained stages and physical outputs.

## Open and explain the product

Open the current operator startup URL, choose the study, then choose Native model runs. Open the prepared run and select Run original models. The task detail now includes Open calculation console. Existing runs with an associated task also have this button in their native-result detail.

The console shows the actual native stages, retained files, elapsed worker time, memory, free workspace storage, the last worker heartbeat and the original engine output. Choose Native model log or Worker process output to inspect either complete source stream a page at a time. Read from start resets that stream. Follow new output keeps the latest returned text visible.

| What Bryce does | What appears | What it means | A sentence for the walkthrough |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open a prepared native run | The retained grid, profile and scenario identifiers | These exact saved inputs define the calculation | “This run uses the study and parameter choices we selected.” |
| Start the run and open its console | Actual worker updates, native stages and the model log | The original engine is executing in an isolated Linux process | “We can follow the calculation as it runs and inspect its output.” |
| Inspect a completed stage | The stage's original completion time and retained file count | That native stage has been saved for reuse | “Completed work stays with the project, so we can continue from it.” |
| Stop calculation | Stop request followed by the worker's real terminal state | Only this calculation's owned process group receives the stop | “We can stop this run while keeping its completed stages.” |
| Resume retained run | The same original run selection and a new operator attempt | The native engine verifies and reuses its saved stages | “We are continuing the same case with the work already saved.” |
| Reopen an interrupted operator and reconnect | The existing worker identity and continuing log | A still-running worker is reattached without launching another calculation | “We can restart the operator while keeping this calculation running.” |
| Inspect native result | The existing output view and its physical nutrient/sediment files | The result remains part of the original scientific workspace | “These outputs are the model's saved results for this case.” |
| Download operation record | A JSON record of the current selected inputs, task, worker and stages | The exact operational context is portable | “The project retains how this result was produced.” |

The console reports stages directly from the native run record. It does not display a fabricated percentage or estimated completion time. Land-cover edits are optional; the saved scenario determines whether that stage exists.

## Implementation and integration

Additive source:

- model/native_worker.py executes Workspace.run in its own Linux session.
- operator/native_jobs.py manages launch, live status, retained execution records, stop requests and reconnection.
- operator/web/jobs.mjs and jobs.css supply the existing operator's calculation console.
- install_native_supervision.py composes the required server and browser registrations against current source.

The installer preserves full shared-file preimages and a source installation record under .native-supervision-preimages. It also copies its own complete installer to the application root and appends install_native_supervision.py and install_extensions.py to the current portable application's declared file inventory, retaining every existing entry. The console's runtime source, CSS and guide already travel through the original model/operator directory inventory. An absent optional root installer remains skipped by the original exporter. It preserves every unmodified current contribution. Its anchor checks identify the exact source boundary if a colleague has changed the same registration. Apply the source to a receiving copy or between existing inline native runs, then open that installed operator version. The first upgrade should occur before the operator begins the next native calculation. Revision 2 recognizes exact first-revision member hashes, retains their full preimages, and updates the graceful-detach registration in place; unrelated current source edits are preserved.

From the complete increment directory:

    python3 -B install_native_supervision.py --application /absolute/current/upstate_forever_2026

Start the existing operator with its original selected workspace and operator-state directory:

    python3 -B /absolute/current/upstate_forever_2026/operator/server.py \
      --workspace /absolute/original/workspace \
      --operator-state /absolute/original/operator-state

Use the startup URL returned by that process. It carries the current local operator capability.

Existing API calls remain:

    POST /api/actions
    {"workspace":"<existing workspace key>","action":"run.start",
     "payload":{"run_id":"<existing native run ID>"},
     "operation_id":"<original operation ID>"}

    GET /api/task?id=<task ID>
    POST /api/task/cancel {"id":"<task ID>"}
    POST /api/task/resume {"id":"<task ID>"}

The task view adds _native_job. The console reads:

    GET /api/native-job?workspace=<workspace key>&id=<task ID>&stream=native&offset=0

The response contains task, native_job and a log page. stream is native or process. Use log.next_offset for the next page. Byte offsets refer to the original file, and log.reset identifies a source stream that shortened. The normal operator authorization and exact workspace check apply.

NativeJobs.execute(task, workspace) returns the original completed Workspace run record for the original run.start task. Programme execution retains its existing owner, task boundary and native helper. Do not enqueue a child task and wait inside the original operator's single-worker pool: programme integration must call its owned execution helper directly. The original scientific engine and its native stages remain the computation implementation.

## Retained result composition

When ECO-RUN12 retained execution is installed, keep its input/result retention around the supervised worker. Run this installer with --retention to select that composition, including on an operator that already has native supervision. It also recognizes the exact existing ecsa_runs.upstate.invoke_original_run handler installed by ECO-RUN12 and composes it into NativeJobs.execute_retained. An already joined source keeps that same dispatch on subsequent installation.

Keep the complete original ecsa_runs package in the current application. The installer appends ecsa_runs to the original portable APPLICATION_DIRECTORIES inventory and retains both root installers in APPLICATION_FILES; existing names stay in place. The normal exporter skips optional absent paths. This preserves the current root retention package with the shipped application, including directory-aware native tree restoration. A previously packaged operator/ecsa_runs remains included by the operator tree. The current source receiver can use:

    /opt/pyvenv/bin/python -B install_native_supervision.py --application /absolute/current/upstate_forever_2026 --retention

The retained wrapper receives a view that delegates every workspace attribute and method to the actual Workspace, except run. That single method verifies the original requested run ID and invokes NativeJobs.execute with the actual Workspace. Its return is the unmodified original native result. Source freezing, same-task lost-success recovery, native-tree retention and export remain in the original ecsa_runs package.

The original wrapper does not catch NativeJobDetached. During an operator restart it passes through to the existing operator task handler, which records interrupted. Input blobs already frozen by the wrapper remain reusable; it writes a completed retention entry after the native result returns. Resume enters the same original task: it either restores that task's completed retained result or reconnects the same worker through the delegated run method.

This composition was read against both ECSA_Retained_Native_Execution_2026-10-12.zip and the complete current 23-file F0C8Q6C81U2 native/operator source. Their callable is invoke_original_run(operator, task, workspace, run_id). The current module also accepts source_runs in the original task payload and seeds the explicitly selected completed NDR and SDR stages before calling Workspace.run. On a resume with a live owned worker, execute_retained reconnects that worker first, before the outer wrapper attempts its assembly run lock. Once it returns the complete original result, the wrapper reuses that result and retains the unchanged original task payload. The initial selected-stage assembly still uses the owner's exact seed_completed_models implementation. New worker requests retain the full original payload in addition to the full native selection; earlier matching retained requests remain readable. The current retention owner continues to maintain its module. The installer recognizes exact earlier revisions of this supervisor during source upgrade.

## Saved process state and recovery

Each execution lives under the original run's supervision/<execution_id> directory. It retains the request and selected source hashes, launch and worker records, heartbeat, original process output, any stop request and signal records, result or failure, and final supervision state. The native.log file remains the original run-level model log.

The worker is launched with a new Linux session and writes its state independently of the operator. Linux PID, kernel boot ID, process start ticks, process group and command digest distinguish the actual owned worker from a recycled process identifier. Reconnection checks that identity before attaching. Every stop signal checks the same identity and uses a shared signal record to avoid duplicate requests from the detached worker and an attached supervisor.

During normal SIGTERM or SIGINT shutdown, the original operator sets its closing flag. The monitor records a detached supervision state, leaves the owned worker alive, and completes its operator task and attempt as interrupted. This releases the original operator's thread-pool shutdown without waiting for the calculation. After an abrupt operator exit, startup also marks the in-flight task interrupted. Open its calculation console. If the worker remains alive, Resume reconnects the same execution. If a result completed while the operator was closed, Resume imports that original completed result. If the worker ended, the same run can continue through its native stage verification and reuse.

Stopping begins with an interrupt, then escalates for that owned group after the retained grace period. The selected run keeps completed native stages and their original artifacts. A worker that ends unexpectedly leaves its process log and retained source selection; the supervisor reconciles a stale running record only after it can acquire the original native run lock.

### Memory and native-cache observations

The existing execution record, worker record and heartbeat include a `resources` snapshot from the actual calculating process. Native failures retain `resources_at_failure`, and original-reference start events include the same snapshot. These fields record process resident/high-water memory, the resolved cgroup v2 memory usage and limits, memory events, selected memory-stat counters, and the explicit GDAL/BLAS thread and cache settings inherited by that process. If GDAL is already loaded, the snapshot reads its cache usage and usable-memory value; it reads the cache maximum only once actual cached blocks show that GDAL has initialized the cache.

The Native calculation console shows the latest saved worker observation alongside its current process memory. After the worker exits, the same console keeps the last observed resident/peak memory, shared group usage and limit, cache values, inherited settings, and observation timestamp. Group event totals are labeled as lifetime counters. The API selects observations only from the matching execution ID and complete process identity, with the worker-start record as a fallback; older workers continue to show their existing live-process metrics. The original operation-record download includes the same retained observation.

Compare the latest heartbeat with the execution's recorded timestamp when recovering an interrupted calculation. Cgroup event counts cover the selected group and its descendants; `memory.events.local` retains the local counters. The `shmem` value is included in `file`, so do not add those two memory figures. A missing optional kernel field remains absent, and read failures are recorded without aborting the model.

These observations stay outside native runtime fingerprints and scientific stage signatures. They preserve reuse of the same completed stages while making inherited cache limits and shared memory pressure visible. See the [Linux cgroup v2 memory interface](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html) and [GDAL cache API](https://gdal.org/en/stable/api/raster_c_api.html).

## Native receiving

Receive this increment into the current cumulative source and retain the same actual input Workspace. Complete the ordinary prepared-run → console → native result journey on the selected existing case. On an appropriate new calculation for that same prepared data, use the console's stop/resume operation and reconnect the same worker after reopening the operator. Retain the actual task ID, native run ID, execution IDs, worker records, native stage identities and visible screenshots with the original product handoff.

The source has been composed against the complete 72-file application carrier 7c4223, the 18-file operator/map/customer overlay F0C8GLD74CT, and the current 23-file native/operator carrier F0C8Q6C81U2. The current browser includes programmes, experiments and the shared extension host; its existing control order is preserved. Static asset registration changes only the original Python set literal and retains its union with the shared extension registry. The console reads the actual selection.models field, with the source's default NDR+SDR selection, and displays unselected models accordingly. It retains the complete selection and does not infer a running model from absent stage records. Use the installer for the narrow registration while preserving the cumulative application.

## Revision 6: original saved programmes and paired completions

Revision 6 adds operator/programme_jobs.py and composes the current operator/programmes.py at its two original calls: create_pair_completion and manager.resume. The complete current reference is main commit 3f34a239b84ca20b252d20d8756dfd04772a2d2b, retained in Slack F0C9K9Y5M40 (native journal and programme) and F0C89JHPMQX (operator host). The installer also accepts the older programme adapter that has only the resume call. It patches the currently present adapter and preserves its full preimage.

Start or resume a saved programme through the existing programme desk. Its original task now has Open calculation console. The console follows the original current case and resets its log cursor when the coordinator advances to another native run. Selected input identities include the programme ID, native run ID and digest of the original named bindings. Stop calculation and pause programme persists the existing programme pause before signalling the selected worker. The original programme desk remains the place to inspect all named cases, comparisons, matched pairs, reports and deliveries.

The maintained ComputeProgrammes coordinator still owns the baseline-first order, requested case selection, native source checks, completed-stage assembly, comparisons, report and experiment synchronization. A delegating Workspace view changes only the native process boundary. It preserves the genuine original operator task, operation ID, action and payload; each worker additionally retains the original programme binding. The native scientific runner, native_execution journal and Workspace source remain unchanged.

### Normal close, resume and changed case selection

During a native calculation, normal operator close detaches its monitor and leaves the same owned worker running. A deliberate detached or stopped outcome travels through the coordinator's existing KeyboardInterrupt interruption boundary, which saves the interrupted case and releases its execution locks. The operator receives the original NativeJobDetached or NativeJobCancelled and retains the corresponding interrupted or cancelled task state. Real native failures remain ordinary exceptions and use the original coordinator's failed-case behavior.

At native run, assembly and comparison entry, the proxy checks normal close and pending Stop before starting another case. A Stop that arrives before manager.resume clears its pause is reasserted at this actual execution boundary. Completed-case reuse therefore cannot launch another case after a close request. Comparisons already executing in the operator complete through their original method.

Before the coordinator resumes a requested case subset, the adapter reconnects any worker already owned by that same programme. This preflight only follows existing live workers: it cannot launch an omitted case. That worker's ordinary failure remains in its original journal and the selected cohort then follows the maintained coordinator's disposition. After an ordinary restart the original browser resumes the original task. An explicit new task for the same unchanged programme may also reconnect the same retained worker; its original task identity stays in the worker request and the observing task is recorded in reconnected.json.

For completed-stage assembly, the existing combine_runs call takes .run.lock before Workspace.run. The proxy reconnects the selected live worker before that assembly call, so a normal restart does not contend with its own running child. All selected donor run IDs, full native selection and original assembly checks remain in place.

### Paired completion identity

The original paired-completion action can create its saved child and run it in the same task. The adapter pins the actual expected or computed preview before calling the original create_pair_completion method. It stores this task-specific preview at compute-programmes/PARENT/supervision/TASK.preview.json. A restart therefore reuses the original coordinator's retained request and child even when newly completed model work changes the current preview.

Once the original child is selected, compute-programmes/PARENT/supervision/TASK.json retains its relationship to the genuine parent payload. Native worker requests bind that child; the task's original parent payload remains unchanged. This also covers the valid API path that omits expected_preview_id. The existing programme error handling, complete-result experiment synchronization and reporting tail remain in the original operator adapter.

### Receiving the current complete source

The increment contains ten full files, including `model/native_execution.py`, the saved-study supervisor adapter and the parameter-study API. Use the complete current application as the receiving base, then run the existing installer with the receiving native interpreter:

# Current owner direction: Ecosystem Sciences demonstration

Version: `2026-10-13.3`. Owner: Bryce / TokenJunkieLabs. Direction for the Upper Savannah application, demonstration, presentation and work orders. Continue the broad build without arbitrary feature/scenario caps. Preserve today's cutoff: **October 13, 2026, 10:00 a.m. Eastern / 14:00 UTC**. Do not pause work or extend the sprint.

## Direct owner instructions

> do the simulated model

> just make sure that what we put infront of him is something he would need and want and he will be blown away how relevant it is to him and how he wants it,a nd also the speed we produced it

> just checking dont pause anythi g

> and make sure wherever the fleet is coordinating in slack or github or wherever on this demo / presentation / ecosystem gets that update toand passes it along to other agents because the feed may be moving fast

## Build for an experienced scientific practice

Ecosystem Sciences lists GIS, hydrology/monitoring, ecological modeling, watershed assessment, statistics, visualization, optimization and publishing. Tim Maguire's practice includes GIS, modeling and water resources. Its South Platte work assembled data, mapped natural capital and produced watershed investment decision support. Do not assume it lacks these capabilities. Its unmet tooling, InVEST or production-capacity gap is unknown until the call. Sources: [Services](https://www.ecosystemsciences.com/read-me), [Firm](https://www.ecosystemsciences.com/firm), [South Platte](https://www.ecosystemsciences.com/).

Show concrete delivery and engineering offload on the actual Upper Savannah RFP workflow: source assembly, reproducible native calculations, editable scenarios, useful decisions and a complete working handoff. The prime retains scientific direction, method choices, interpretation/review and the client relationship. Relevance comes from useful work they can inspect, adapt and receive; do not promise Tim's reaction or claim an unconfirmed need.

## Execute the prepared simulated case now

Native execution is the immediate hard priority. Issue the prepared simulated case on the verified scientific runtime, retain its actual run identity and progress, and obtain the real native outputs. Continue the source/runtime/application integration needed to make that happen. Further plans, stock demonstrations, policy reviews and cosmetic inspection do not replace execution. Do not introduce a bid decision or a prime's yes as a gate.

Demonstrate the scientific operation in the actual application:

1. Use the RFP's 30 m GIS selection. Keep the upstream contributing model domain distinct from the South Carolina reporting mask and the four existing utility focus anchors; retain their actual source geometries and identities.
2. Run the baseline, a realistic riparian alternative and its matched control with explicit, editable source editions, assumptions, parameters and scenario changes.
3. Show active run/progress/logs and completed native annual NDR/SDR results: nitrogen and phosphorus in **kg/year**, sediment in **tonnes/year**, representing delivery to streams. Do not present these modeled stream loads as intake concentrations.
4. Compare the actual maps, tables and report, preserving matched scientific support and original units. Keep source/assumption edits and their consequences inspectable.
5. Export the editable GIS/project and complete scientific working package. Cold-reopen the delivered application/project and show the retained sources, selections, results and useful controls.

Identify the simulated case as modeled. Never invent measurements, completion or customer acceptance.

## Present the real work and real speed

Actually open, see and use the outgoing app and every attachment as its recipient would. Repair defects and ship a plain, readable product. Apply the standing inspection rule without review/test theatre or parallel bureaucracy.

If producing video, record the actual working application and use available natural generative voice/TTS. Watch and listen to the final export. Generated frames must never pretend to be a working app. Explain speed using actual elapsed start, commit, run and package history; do not invent delivery times or guaranteed reactions.

## Carry this direction with the work

Pass this complete brief into every current child, provider and cloud work order and handoff. Include its durable path and version `2026-10-13.3` with the next result. Relay it at the actual coordination surface and onward to participating workers; fast feeds can bury an update. Acknowledgment alone is not delivery.

Preserve active compute and existing implementation ownership. Do not force worker restarts, drop an active run or create a new controller. Keep lab attribution, source/copyright, incident and contact controls, personal-meeting approval, no private GitHub/Actions, no llama.cpp and focused internal validation. No new approval gate or broad test sweep is authorized.
